chapter: WDSU radio and the New Orleans scene
title: Record librarian at WDSU, Sharkey and Frank Assunto
summary: As WDSU record librarian he heard Sharkey's tapes and once sat in on bass for a tape with Frank Assunto when the bassist did not show up.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Well, yeah, I knew him while I was working at WDSU. I was a record librarian. Of course, Sharky always came in and played tapes for recordings, you know, for Capitol, wasn't it? Yeah. Yeah. Mm-hmm. So I got to hear him through that and I learned a lot about jazz, which I didn't know, you know. And, of course, being a librarian in a record library radio station is quite an experience. And I think that's how I got to learn a lot of things. And, oh, by the way, you know, one day Frank Assunto was due to make a tape for overseas servicemen, you know, and all the guys showed up except the bass player. So they called his home. They called his parents and they couldn't find them anywhere. Well, they finally thought, well, he must be in some movie in town because he couldn't find them anywhere else. And he liked to watch Western movies. Well, they didn't have time to go and search every movie house in New Orleans. So Pete Lotteman, who happened to be musical director of WDSU, says, well, why don't you use Rudy? He's a bass player. He's right here. So Frank says, crazy, man. So I sat in and I played a tape with Frank Assunto, man. That was a real joy, believe me. I was very happy to do it. Of course, it was a benefit and all that. It really made me feel great, you know.
Was anybody in Chaggy's band outstanding?
Well, they all were outstanding. I mean, to me, the whole thing was just one outstanding body.
Let's put it that way. He was doing a lot of engagements in the Pond House in Chicago. Does he still go there now? Or does he bother to go out? I don't know.
He traveled some. I don't know if he's been up there like that.
He still does. Well, anyway, I was always looking forward when he came to WDSU because he was making the recording sessions and sessions, you know. I really enjoyed that. It was a kick.
